chapters.1.summary: After Joshua dies, Israel asks the LORD who should fight first. Judah goes up with Simeon and defeats Adoni-Bezek. Caleb’s daughter Achsah again receives her springs. Judah takes the hill country but cannot drive out the plain’s iron chariots. Benjamin does not drive the Jebusites from Jerusalem. Joseph’s house takes Bethel with help from a man of the city. Manasseh, Ephraim, Zebulun, Asher, and Naphtali leave Canaanites in their towns. When Israel grows strong, it puts them to forced labor.
chapters.1.lds: Which tribes drive out their neighbors? Which leave them in place or force them to work (verses 27–33)?
chapters.2.summary: The LORD’s angel comes to Bochim and says Israel has not obeyed. So the nations will stay as thorns and their gods as a snare. The people weep. The account then looks back: Israel served the LORD while Joshua and the elders lived. A new generation arose that did not know the LORD or his works. They served the Baals, and the LORD gave them to raiders. He raised up judges to save them, but after each judge they turned back. So the LORD left the nations to test Israel.
chapters.2.lds: Come, Follow Me studies repentance and the Lord’s repeated willingness to receive people who return. What did the new generation not know (verse 10)?
chapters.3.summary: The LORD leaves several nations to test Israel. Israel marries among them and serves their gods. A king of Mesopotamia rules them eight years, and Othniel, of Caleb’s family, saves them. Then Eglon king of Moab rules Israel eighteen years. The LORD raises up Ehud, a left-handed man of Benjamin. Ehud hides a sword on his right thigh and kills Eglon in private. He escapes, calls Israel to fight, and Moab is subdued. Shamgar later kills six hundred Philistines with an ox goad.
chapters.3.lds: The older Church manual studies Israel’s return to God during trouble. What detail about Ehud does verse 15 give?
chapters.4.summary: Israel does evil again, and Jabin king of Canaan oppresses them twenty years. His general Sisera has nine hundred iron chariots. Deborah, a prophetess, judges Israel under a palm tree. She tells Barak that the LORD commands him to gather ten thousand men. Barak will go only if she goes with him. She agrees but says a woman will get the honor. The LORD routs Sisera’s army, and Sisera flees on foot to Jael’s tent. Jael gives him milk and kills him with a tent peg as he sleeps.
chapters.4.lds: Come, Follow Me studies Deborah’s influence and asks how faith can help other people act. What does Deborah tell Barak about the honor of the victory (verse 9)?
chapters.5.summary: Deborah and Barak sing after the victory. They praise leaders and people who offered themselves willingly. The song recalls empty roads and villages before Deborah arose. It praises the tribes that came: Ephraim, Benjamin, Zebulun, Issachar, and Naphtali. It asks why Reuben, Gilead, Dan, and Asher stayed home. The stars and the river Kishon fought against Sisera. Jael is called most blessed of women for killing him. The song ends with Sisera’s mother waiting at her window for him.
chapters.5.lds: The older manual studies willing service and courage. Read the poem’s celebration beside its depiction of harm. Which tribes stayed away, according to verses 16–17?
chapters.6.summary: Midian raids Israel for seven years and strips the land at harvest. Israel cries out, and a prophet reminds them they did not listen. The LORD’s angel finds Gideon threshing wheat in a winepress to hide it. He calls Gideon a mighty man and sends him to save Israel. Gideon says his family is the poorest and he is the least. At night he tears down his father’s altar to Baal. His father Joash tells the angry town to let Baal defend himself. Gideon gathers an army and twice asks for a sign with a fleece.
chapters.6.lds: Come, Follow Me studies trust when God’s instructions differ from what a person expects. Whose altar must Gideon pull down first (verse 25)?
chapters.7.summary: Gideon camps with thirty-two thousand men. The LORD says they are too many, or Israel will boast that it saved itself. The fearful go home, and ten thousand remain. At the water the LORD keeps only the three hundred who lap from their hands. Gideon sneaks to the enemy camp and hears a man tell a dream of defeat. He gives each man a trumpet, a jar, and a torch. At night they blow, break the jars, and shout. The Midianites turn on each other and flee.
chapters.7.lds: The Church lesson studies reliance on God. Why does the LORD shrink Gideon’s army (verse 2)?
chapters.8.summary: Ephraim complains at being called late, and Gideon calms them with praise. He chases two Midianite kings across the Jordan with his tired three hundred. Succoth and Penuel refuse him bread. He captures the kings, then punishes Succoth’s elders and kills the men of Penuel. He kills the two kings for the death of his brothers. Israel asks him to rule, and he says the LORD will rule. But he collects gold earrings and makes an ephod that Israel worships. After his death Israel turns to the Baals and forgets his family.
chapters.8.lds: Come, Follow Me studies trust. The older manual also warns about the ephod and acknowledges the account’s change after victory. What did Gideon’s ephod become (verse 27)?
chapters.9.summary: Abimelech, Gideon’s son by a woman of Shechem, asks Shechem to make him ruler. They give him silver, and he hires men and kills his seventy brothers. Only the youngest, Jotham, escapes. Jotham shouts a story from Mount Gerizim about trees choosing a king. The olive, fig, and vine refuse, and the bramble accepts. Three years later Shechem turns against Abimelech. He destroys the city and burns its tower with the people inside. At Thebez a woman drops a millstone on his head, and he dies.
chapters.9.lds: The manual studies Jotham’s warning. What does the bramble offer the trees in verse 15, and what does it threaten?
chapters.10.summary: Tola judges Israel twenty-three years, and Jair twenty-two. Israel again serves the gods of the nations around it. The LORD gives them to the Philistines and Ammonites for eighteen years. Israel cries out and admits its sin. The LORD lists his past rescues and says he will save them no more. He tells them to cry to the gods they chose. Israel confesses again, puts away the foreign gods, and serves the LORD. He can bear their misery no longer, and Ammon gathers for war.
chapters.10.lds: The manual studies the return to God. What did Israel do in verse 16 after the LORD’s answer?
chapters.11.summary: Jephthah is a strong fighter, but his brothers drive him out as a prostitute’s son. When Ammon attacks, the elders of Gilead ask him to lead them. He agrees on condition that he stay their head. He sends Ammon’s king a long case from history that Israel took no Ammonite land. The king does not listen. Jephthah vows to offer whatever first comes from his house if he wins. He wins, and his only daughter comes out dancing to meet him. She asks two months to mourn, and he does to her as he vowed.
chapters.11.lds: The older manual reads the vow as lifelong service. Hayes reads it as sacrifice. The readings differ over the daughter’s fate. What does Jephthah say when he sees her (verse 35)?
chapters.12.summary: The men of Ephraim are angry that Jephthah fought Ammon without them. They threaten to burn his house. Jephthah says he called and they did not come. Gilead fights Ephraim and takes the Jordan crossings. Each fleeing man is told to say “Shibboleth.” An Ephraimite says “Sibboleth” and is killed. Forty-two thousand of Ephraim die. Jephthah judges six years, and Ibzan, Elon, and Abdon follow him.
chapters.12.lds: The manual compares the conflict with Gideon’s earlier response. How did Gideon answer Ephraim’s complaint in 8:1–3?
chapters.13.summary: Israel does evil, and the Philistines rule them forty years. The LORD’s angel appears to the childless wife of Manoah of Dan. She will bear a son who must be a Nazirite from birth. She must drink no wine, and no razor may touch his head. Manoah prays for the man to return, and the angel comes again to the woman. Manoah offers a goat, and the angel goes up in the altar flame. Manoah fears they will die for seeing God. His wife says God would not accept their offering and then kill them.
chapters.13.lds: Come, Follow Me studies covenant faithfulness. The manual treats the angel as God’s messenger rather than naming him as Christ. How does Manoah’s wife answer his fear in verse 23?
chapters.14.summary: Samson sees a Philistine woman in Timnah and demands her as his wife. His parents object, not knowing the LORD is seeking an occasion against the Philistines. On the way Samson tears a young lion apart with his hands. Later he finds honey in its carcass and eats it. At his wedding feast he bets thirty guests they cannot solve his riddle. They threaten to burn his wife and her father’s house unless she gets the answer. She weeps until Samson tells her, and she tells them. Samson kills thirty men to pay the bet, and his wife is given away.
chapters.14.lds: The Church lesson studies Samson’s choices. How do the threats in verse 15 affect what his wife does?
chapters.15.summary: Samson returns for his wife and learns she was given to another man. He ties torches to three hundred foxes and burns the Philistines’ grain. The Philistines burn his wife and her father. Samson strikes them down and hides in a rock cleft. Three thousand men of Judah come to hand him over. He lets them bind him, then snaps the ropes when the Spirit comes on him. He kills a thousand men with a donkey’s jawbone. He is thirsty and calls on the LORD, and God opens a spring.
chapters.15.lds: The older Church manual studies Samson’s strength and his request for water. Who pays for the burned fields in verse 6?
chapters.16.summary: Samson visits a prostitute in Gaza and carries off the city gates at midnight. He loves Delilah, and Philistine lords pay her to learn his secret. Three times he lies to her, and each time she tests it. She presses him daily until he tells her about his uncut hair. She has his head shaved while he sleeps, and the LORD leaves him. The Philistines blind him and make him grind grain in prison. At a feast for their god Dagon they bring him out for sport. He prays, pushes down the two pillars, and dies with them.
chapters.16.lds: Come, Follow Me studies covenant faithfulness. The older manual distinguishes Samson’s gift of strength from consistent moral conduct. What does Samson ask for in verse 28?
chapters.17.summary: Micah of Ephraim admits he took his mother’s eleven hundred pieces of silver. She blesses him and has part of it made into an idol. Micah has a shrine, an ephod, and household gods, and makes a son his priest. In those days Israel had no king, and everyone did what seemed right. A young Levite from Bethlehem comes looking for a place. Micah hires him for ten pieces of silver a year, clothes, and food. The Levite becomes his priest. Micah says the LORD will surely do him good now.
chapters.17.lds: The manual reads this episode as part of religious decline. Why does Micah think the LORD will do him good (verse 13)?
chapters.18.summary: The tribe of Dan is looking for land. Five scouts stay at Micah’s house and ask his Levite for a word from God. They find Laish, a quiet town with no defender. Six hundred armed Danites set out. On the way they take Micah’s idol, ephod, and gods, and invite the priest along. The priest is glad to serve a tribe in place of one man. Micah chases them and is warned off. Dan burns Laish, kills its people, renames it Dan, and sets up the idol.
chapters.18.lds: The older manual places the migration in the book’s closing decline. Read the inhabitants’ loss beside the migrants’ claim. What does Micah say was taken from him (verse 24)?
chapters.19.summary: A Levite’s concubine leaves him and returns to her father in Bethlehem. He goes to bring her back and is kept there for days. On the way home they pass a foreign town and reach Gibeah of Benjamin. Only an old man takes them in. Men of the city surround the house and demand the Levite. He pushes his concubine out to them, and they abuse her all night. In the morning she lies dead at the door. He cuts her body into twelve pieces and sends them through Israel.
chapters.19.lds: The older Church manual describes the harm caused by Israel’s loss of moral care. What do those who see the Levite’s message say (verse 30)?
chapters.20.summary: All Israel gathers at Mizpah, four hundred thousand armed men. The Levite tells what Gibeah did but leaves out his own part. The tribes demand that Benjamin hand over the guilty men. Benjamin refuses and gathers its army. Israel asks God who should go first and loses twenty-two thousand men. They weep, ask again, and lose eighteen thousand more. After fasting and offerings, they set an ambush and win on the third day. Benjamin loses twenty-five thousand men, and only six hundred escape.
chapters.20.lds: The manual describes the near destruction of Benjamin. Compare the Levite’s report in verses 4–6 with 19:25. What does he leave out?
chapters.21.summary: Israel had sworn not to give daughters to Benjamin. Now the people weep that a tribe is nearly gone. Six hundred Benjamite men survive and need wives. Israel finds that Jabesh Gilead sent no one to the assembly. They kill its people and take four hundred young women for Benjamin. That is not enough. The elders tell the remaining men to seize dancers at the Shiloh feast. The book ends: there was no king, and everyone did what seemed right.
chapters.21.lds: The older Church manual condemns the seizure of women as wives. What do the elders plan to tell the women’s fathers (verse 22)?
